headline: Microsoft cuts Family plan OneDrive from 6 TB to 2 TB
dek: Copilot opens to five more members as storage shrinks, per Canaltech and Tecmundo.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A smaller pool, a wider Copilot
body: Microsoft is cutting the OneDrive storage in its Microsoft 365 Family plan from 6 TB to a shared 2 TB pool. Copilot, its AI assistant in Office, opens to up to five other people on the plan (Canaltech, Tecmundo).
New subscriptions get the change now. Existing subscribers see it at the first renewal on or after May 2, 2027, and Microsoft says it will email them first (Canaltech, Tecmundo).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: From individual to shared
s3.body: The Family plan used to give each member their own space. Now the whole group draws from one pool (Canaltech, Tecmundo).

points.t: Up to six people had 1 TB each. One 2 TB pool replaces that, a cut of more than 66% (Canaltech).
Account holders can share Copilot with five other members and manage access for younger ones (Tecmundo).
Separate limits for chat, reasoning and images give way to one shared allowance; extra credits can be bought (Canaltech, Tecmundo).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Less room, more AI access
body: A member who stores little frees space for one who stores more, Microsoft says, but the group total is far smaller than before (Tecmundo).
Families near the old ceiling must trim files or buy extra capacity, up to 10 TB. Microsoft has promised an adjustment period before removing any files (Canaltech).

items.t: The change already applies to new Microsoft 365 Family subscriptions (Canaltech, Tecmundo).
Existing subscribers are affected from the first renewal on or after May 2, with an email notice at least 30 days ahead (Tecmundo).
Premium moves to the same 2 TB pool, and Pro offers 5 TB to split among users (Canaltech).

caption.hook: Microsoft will cut OneDrive in the 365 Family plan from 6 TB to a shared 2 TB and open Copilot to five more members.
body: The change was detailed in a notice to subscribers and first reported by The Verge this week, according to Canaltech and Tecmundo. Each of up to six people on an account had 1 TB before.

Tecmundo reports Microsoft promised temporary storage bonuses and transition support for the most affected subscribers. Age-based limits on content generation stay, and parents manage them in the family safety dashboard.
Canaltech adds that files above the new quota will not be deleted right away.
